title: 3D Tree Hierarchy (Radial Expansion)
prompt:
Use Three.js to display hardcoded tree data in a 3D radial/hierarchical layout (in the style of an organizational chart or directory tree).

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following import map in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Data]
(1) Hardcode a tree with exactly 50 nodes and a maximum depth of 4 (root depth is 0).

[Layout and Rendering]
(2) 3D radial tree: child nodes expand around their parent in a fan-shaped/conical arrangement, with connections rendered as line segments or thin cylinders.
(3) Clicking a node expands or collapses its subtree (collapse it if it is already expanded).
(4) id="searchFilter": a text input that filters by node label (hide non-matching subtrees or gray them out; visibleNodes must reflect the current number of visible nodes).

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  nodeCount: number,
  visibleNodes: number,
  expandedNodes: number,
  selectedNode: null | string | number,
  searchFilter: string
}

nodeCount must always be 50; after collapsing, visibleNodes < 50; expandedNodes is the current count of expanded internal nodes (the implementation must define this clearly and keep it consistent with the UI).

Output a single HTML file that runs when opened directly in a browser.
